newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, MARCH 10-SUNDAY, MARCH 16 (PAGE 1/3 - MONDAY-TUESDAY).
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, MARCH 10-SUNDAY, MARCH 16 (PAGE 1/3 - MONDAY-TUESDAY).

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (Monday-Friday); solemn session for the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome (Wednesday); debate on transit customs fraud (Wednesday); debates on EU agreements with Eastern Europe (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - EU inter-governmental conference representatives meet (Monday-Tuesday).
BRUSSELS - EU transport ministers meet (Tuesday-Wednesday); discussions focus on proposal to modify rules on lorry cab tachographs and harmonisation of summertime rules for changing clocks.
STRASBOURG - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday); discussions on draft directive on taxation of energy products and on media ownership in the internal market.
BRUSSELS - Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (Wednesday-Thursday).
BRUSSELS - EU internal market ministers meet (Thursday); open debate on Commission communication on the impact and effectiveness of the internal market.

THE HAGUE - German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel meet Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo (Thursday); discussions focus on state of the inter-governmental conference, EU and NATO enlargement, planned single currency and key foreign policy issues - followed by a news conference.
ROTTERDAM - EU social affairs ministers hold informal meeting (Friday and Saturday); discussions focus on unemployment.

APELDOORN, Netherland - EU foreign ministers hold informal meeting (Saturday and Sunday); discussions focus on how to proceed with negotiations with 10 former communist bloc countries that have been promised eventual EU membership.
MONDAY, MARCH 10
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EU inter-governmental conference representatives meet (and Tuesday).
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (to Friday).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1700/1600 GMT) Order of business.
- Announcement of the list of subjects for the debate on topical and urgent subjects of major importance.
- Marlies Mosiek-Urbahn report on the capital adequacy of investment firms and credit institutions (solvency ratio).
- Marlies Mosiek-Urbahn report on the supplementary supervision of insurance undertakings in an insurance group.
- Nicole Fontaine report on the report to EP and Council on the state of application of the general system for the recognition of higher education diplomas.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1900/1800 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
Agriculture;
Budget;
Energy;
External Economic Relations;
Legal Affairs;
Environment;
Development;
Civil Liberties;
Budgetary Control;
Institutional Affairs.
LUXEMBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Benelux Consultative Interparliamentary Council holds news conference pior to the conference on the euro (1000/0900 GMT). Venue: Chambre des Deputes.
TUESDAY, MARCH 11
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Transport Council (1000/0900 GMT) (and Wednesday).
Agenda includes:
- Air Transport:

- Proposal for a Council directive amending Council directive 92/14/EEC on the limitation of the operation of aeroplanes covered by Part II, Chapter 2, volume I of Annex 16 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation, second edition (1988).
- Levies on aircraft fuel.
- Orientation debate on air traffic management and European organisation in civil aviation security.
- Ground transport:
- Common position on a control apparatus for inroad transport (tachograph) - proposal for regulation modifying regulation 3821/85 and directive 85/599/EEC.
- Resolution on telematic deployment in road transport, especially in electronic perception of fees.
- Proposal for a Council regulation concerning the granting of Community financial assistance for actions to promote combined goods transport (PACT).
- Proposal for a Council directive on the charging of heavy goods vehicles for the use of certain infrastructures - orientation debate.
- Other measures:
- Proposal for an EP and Council directive on summertime arrangements common position.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EU inter-governmental conference representatives meet (second of two days). (Possibly) Closing news conference.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Monti chairs first taxation political meeting.
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (second of five days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Announcement of the motions for resolutions tabled on topical and urgent subject of major importance.
- Susan Waddington report on the Commission's white paper on education and training - towards the learning society.
- Wim van Velzen report on the Commission's green paper on living and working in the information society: People First.
- Mair Eluned Morgan on the information society, culture and education.
- Oral Question to the Council on drift nets.
- Joint debate:
- Arlindo Cunha on EC/Angola fisheries agreement.
- Allan Macartney on EC/Guinea fisheries agreement.
- Dagmar Roth-Behrendt on animal experiments in the field of cosmetic products.
- Leen van der Waal report on the limitation of the operation of aeroplanes.
- Recommendation for second reading by Peter Liese on North-South cooperation in the campaign against drugs and drug addiction.
- Recommendation for second reading by Nordmann on aid for population policies and programmes in the developping countries.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Votes on: reports under the cooperation, codecision and assent procedures; motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed.
- Announcement of the list of motions for resolutions selected for the debate on topical and urgent matters of major importance.
- (1730/1630 GMT) Commission question time.
- (1900/1800 GMT) Political group meetings.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1730/1630 GMT) Economic;
Employment;
Fisheries.

BRUSSELS - International Accounting Standards Committee holds conference on "International accounting standards - Implications for major European corporations" (1000/0900 GMT) (and Wednesday). Venue: Sheraton Hotel. Contact: Clare McSheaffrey, Touchstone Exhibitions and Conferences (44) 181 332 0044.
